title: The 8 Levels of Procrastination
house: A bustling metropolitan university district where fruit and vegetable people rush through rain-slicked concrete plazas, neon-lit libraries, and endless coffee shops.
catchphrase: The number on my forehead never lies.
links: Level 2 mentions buying coffee from a tired strawberry barista.
Level 4 borrows a highlighter from a calm blueberry law student.
Level 6 walks past an exhausted bell pepper crying in the Metro.

levels.open_loop: What was the final urgent warning written on the mysterious sticky note?

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs loudly at my panicked breakdown in the library aisle.

levels.name: Leo, 20, History Student
levels.story: Fourteen days left and my essay is just a blank white screen. I'm Leo, a soft, fuzzy peach with grease-stained sweatpants and a constantly flickering digital forehead. I stared at the blinking cursor while my roommate yelled, You are going to fail this entire semester. I told myself I had plenty of time for 4,000 words. But then my forehead number shifted instantly. My hands started shaking as the campus library clock chimed midnight. What was the final urgent warning written on the mysterious sticky note? You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Maya, 21, Bio Major
levels.story: Seven days left and I finally opened the textbook for the first time. I am Maya, a bright yellow lemon wearing a neat cardigan and clutching an iced latte bought from the strawberry barista. I told myself, One week is basically a whole eternity of productive focus. But my friend gasped when she saw my screen and whispered, That source list is completely fake. My forehead countdown blinked faster, and my heart dropped into my shoes. Why did the professor cross out my entire bibliography in red ink? You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Sam, 22, Econ Student
levels.story: Seventy-two hours left and the caffeine has completely stopped working. I am Sam, a tough brown coconut wearing a slightly wrinkled dress shirt and carrying a heavy backpack. I stared at the spreadsheet and my study group leader shouted, You haven't even touched the financial models yet. Panic surged through my wooden shell as I tried to type faster. My digital forehead number plummeted instantly. What hidden file did I accidentally delete from my desktop? You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Chloe, 19, Art History
levels.story: Twenty-four hours left and my room looks like a paper tornado hit it. I am Chloe, a smooth green avocado wearing an oversized vintage sweater and paint-splattered jeans. I borrowed a highlighter from a calm blueberry law student just moments before my printer jammed completely. My mom called me on speakerphone and screamed, How could you leave everything to the very last day. Tears welled in my eyes as the deadline loomed closer. Who sent the anonymous email threatening to report my rough draft? You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Ben, 23, Physics Major
levels.story: Six hours left and my brain is operating on pure unfiltered adrenaline. I am Ben, a spiky green broccoli wearing a zipped-up athletic jacket and carrying a massive physics tome. I sprinted across the rainy quad past the bell pepper crying in the Metro station. The head proctor looked at his watch and announced coldly, Anyone arriving after midnight will be locked out permanently. My digital timer flashed a violent warning color. Why was the examination hall door locked ten minutes early? You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Zoe, 21, Chemistry Student
levels.story: Sixty minutes left and my hands won't stop shaking. I am Zoe, a dragon fruit with striking pink skin and neon green spikes, wearing a sleek black turtleneck. I rushed past an exhausted bell pepper crying in the Metro and dropped my entire pen collection on the concrete. A passing senior sneered at me, You are definitely going to fail this organic chemistry final. My forehead display flashed sixty red minutes of pure terror. What secret formula was written on the back of my admission ticket? You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Oliver, 24, Grad Assistant
levels.story: Zero seconds left and I hit the submit button right as the server crashed. I am Oliver, a wise purple eggplant wearing a tailored professor vest and round spectacles. I looked out at the lecture hall filled with peach, lemon, coconut, avocado, broccoli, dragon fruit, and pumpkin students who survived the chaos. The dean smiled and told me, Your unconventional procrastination method somehow saved the entire department budget. My forehead timer finally turned a brilliant emerald green. What topic should we explore next in our series?
